records.derivation: Check all 3 disjoint chord pairings without assuming one vertex order across the whole interval. QP and SR cannot be parallel because cot(x)+cos(x)<-1 while tan(x)+sin(x)>-1. Multiplying by the nonzero sin(x)*cos(x) yields cos(x)*sin(x)=cos(x)+sin(x), since cos(x) and sin(x) cannot be equal. Their sum u is negative and satisfies u²=1+2 u, so u=1-sqrt(2). For two distinct stationary points, the smaller point has derivative sign+ then-, so is a genuine local maximum, and three real roots require its value nonnegative. The triple-root limiting case is handled explicitly, not called an extremum: at the optimum the derivative is 3*(x-sqrt(3))² and has no sign change. Eliminating b gives f(u)=a*(u²-1)-2 u³>=0, hence u>1 and a>=2 u³/(u²-1)>=3*sqrt(3). The latter inequality follows from(u-sqrt(3))²*(2 u+sqrt(3))>=0. When the stationary points coincide, three real roots force the explicit triple-root case rather than a false local-maximum inference. Choice B.
records.qualification: The flat triple root at the minimizing parameter is a boundary case, not a local extremum. The recorded derivative route is valid only with that explicit branch and the separate cubic/root argument above. The corrected node alone does not certify three real roots.
